title: Enhancing the resilience of the gilt repo market – discussion paper feedback statement
summary: The Bank of England published a feedback statement summarising industry responses to its September 2025 discussion paper on gilt repo market resilience. Respondents broadly supported the Bank's objective but raised concerns about the proportionality and potential negative spillovers of proposals for mandatory central clearing or non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts. The Bank indicated it will continue exploring structural changes to enable greater adoption of central clearing while addressing identified obstacles.
key_points: Respondents broadly agreed with the Bank's assessment that gilt repo market dynamics can generate liquidity imbalances in stress conditions.
Industry highlighted access barriers, operational constraints and cost considerations as making central clearing unfeasible for most participants under current market structure.
Most respondents opposed mandatory central clearing, favouring incentives for voluntary adoption such as cross-product margining, new access models, and expanding acceptable collateral pools.
Most respondents were not supportive of non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts on non-centrally cleared repo, noting these would raise funding costs and potentially divert activity to other markets.
Proposed additional resilience measures included innovations to the Contingent Non-Bank Financial Institutions Repo Facility (CNRF) and the Short-Term Repo (STR) facility.
The Bank will continue assessing and designing policies to enhance resilience, exploring market structure changes to enable greater central clearing adoption.
why_it_matters: The gilt repo market is critical infrastructure for UK financial stability, government cash management, and market-based funding. Historical stress events (March 2020 'dash for cash', September 2022 LDI episode) demonstrated how market dysfunction can transmit to the real economy. This feedback statement signals the Bank's regulatory direction on potential reforms to central clearing and margin requirements that could affect dealer balance sheets, hedge fund funding costs, and overall market liquidity dynamics.
market_structure_context: The document discusses structural changes to the gilt repo market including proposals for greater central clearing, minimum haircuts on non-centrally cleared transactions, and innovations to the Contingent Non-Bank Financial Institutions Repo Facility (CNRF) and Sterling Monetary Framework (SMF). The market structure has shifted with leveraged hedge funds increasing participation while pension funds have become less active.
